mcq.q: An ad valorem import duty of 10% is levied on a machine imported at a value of ₹50,000. The duty payable is:
mcq.explain: An ad valorem tariff is a percentage of the value of the imported good. Duty = 10% of ₹50,000 = ₹5,000. A specific tariff, by contrast, is a fixed amount per unit (for example ₹200 per unit), regardless of the value of the good.
mcq.topic: Tariffs: meaning, specific and ad valorem
mcq.fast: Ad valorem = % of value; specific = fixed amount per unit.

mcq.q: A compound duty of 5% of value plus ₹100 per unit is levied on 20 units imported at ₹1,000 each. The total duty is:
mcq.explain: A compound tariff combines an ad valorem and a specific duty. Ad valorem part = 5% × (20 × ₹1,000) = ₹1,000. Specific part = 20 × ₹100 = ₹2,000. Total duty = ₹1,000 + ₹2,000 = ₹3,000.
mcq.fast: Compound = ad valorem part + specific part.

mcq.q: A duty imposed to offset subsidies given by a foreign government to its exporters is a:
mcq.explain: A countervailing duty is levied on imports that benefit from subsidies in the exporting country, to neutralise the unfair price advantage. An anti-dumping duty is levied when a foreign firm sells in the importing market at a price below its normal value and this injures domestic producers.
mcq.topic: Trigger-price responses: anti-dumping and countervailing duties
mcq.fast: Foreign subsidy -> countervailing; below normal value -> anti-dumping.

mcq.q: When a country imposes a tariff on an imported good, in the importing country:
options: The domestic price rises, consumption falls and domestic production rises
mcq.explain: A tariff raises the price of imports and of the good in the domestic market. Consumers buy less, while domestic producers, protected by the higher price, produce more. Imports fall, the government earns tariff revenue, and there is a deadweight loss of efficiency for the economy.
mcq.fast: Tariff: P up, consumption down, domestic output up, imports down.

mcq.q: An arrangement under which the exporting country itself limits the quantity of a good it exports to an importing country is a:
options: Import quota set by the importing country
mcq.explain: A voluntary export restraint (VER) is a limit on exports that the exporting country "voluntarily" agrees to, usually under pressure from the importing country. An import quota, by contrast, is set by the importing country. VERs are a type of non-tariff measure.
mcq.fast: Exporter limits itself = VER; importer limits = quota.

mcq.q: Measures that require imported food to meet standards for food safety and animal and plant health are:
mcq.explain: SPS measures protect human, animal and plant life or health — for example limits on pesticide residues or rules on disease-free meat. Technical barriers to trade (TBT) cover other product standards, labelling and testing. Both are technical non-tariff measures.
mcq.topic: Non-tariff measures (NTMs) and NTBs; technical measures (SPS, TBT)
